notes: Summary: Marshlight is evaluating Dedicated capacity for low-latency customer-facing assistants and reranking pipelines tied to trading UX.
Primary asks: deterministic p95/p99 guarantees for peak daytime traffic and an agreed measurement methodology (client vs server timing).
POC plan: 3-week POC on Redwood Dedicated. Week1: integration + correctness; Week2: synthetic load & latency baselining; Week3: production-representative replay + 3rd-party latency audit.
Deliverable: latency report with p50/p95/p99 by request size and streaming vs non-streaming flows.
operational_details: Latency SLO draft (Marshlight asks): non-streaming complete-response p50 < 40ms, p95 < 180ms, p99 < 420ms for payloads <=2k tokens.
Streaming SLO draft: first-byte p50 < 25ms, first-byte p95 < 120ms; sustained streaming increments p95 < 60ms.
Marshlight insists client-side measurement be ground truth for user-perceived latency but will accept server-side enforcement if correlation delta < 5% at 95th percentile.
Throughput planning: baseline 100 req/s, peak 350 req/s spikes, avg request 800 tokens; initial reserved request: 12 A100-equivalent GPUs with burst to 16 for 1-hour windows.
measurement_alignment_notes: Definitions proposed: client-side end-to-end = SDK send timestamp -> SDK first-byte or completion timestamp.
Server-side processing = server ingress receive -> server egress first-byte.
Network delta = client end-to-end minus server processing. Use to isolate network/regional routing impact.
Agreement: instrument SDK to include client send timestamp and correlate with server request-id header; both sides to NTP-sync clocks and publish nightly p50/p95/p99 histograms during POC.
Exclusions agreed: retries >2 attempts, 5xx failures, requests >8k tokens causing model fallback unless pre-approved, warm-up periods for new model variants (30 minutes).
sla_and_contract_notes: Penalty structure draft: p95 breach for 2+ days -> 2% daily credit; sustained p99 breach escalate to 5% daily credit; monthly aggregate capped at 10% negotiable.
Monitoring: Redwood to expose raw latency histograms by model variant, region, streaming vs non-streaming and provide CSV dumps for audit.
Runbook: 24/7 incident channel, dedicated SE on-call during POC, quarterly SLA reviews post-procurement.
Legal redlines: measurement ownership clarity, blackout windows, maintenance notification windows (72h for non-critical), RCA timeline (48h for high-severity).
reserved_capacity_planning: Sizing calc: target 300 req/s sustained with avg 800 tokens -> modeled 12 GPUs (A100 equiv) with 20% headroom.
Redwood suggested initial 10 reserved + autoscale burst to 14; Marshlight prefers fixed reserved pool + scheduled burst for cost predictability.
Throughput guarantee ask: baseline throughput guarantee at 95% of provisioned pool over rolling 30-day window; burst capacity is contracted optionally.
Model variants: use q4/q8 quantized variants for reranking to reduce GPU footprint; preserve fp16 for chat flows with strict latency SLOs.
final_comments: Marshlight wants an auditable user-perceived latency metric (client-side) but will accept server-side enforcement if correlation within 5% at 95th percentile.
Main procurement blocker: legal alignment on credit caps and exclusions for third-party network segments (CDN).
Next meeting: 2026-03-18 to review contract redlines and kick off POC. SE to supply tokenized request set and SDK instrumentation checklist prior to meeting.
